rationale: First candidate for this selection (no inputs/previous-feedback.txt and no previous candidate manifest exist). The objective ttft_ms (clean baseline 24.611 ms, project.json) covers only the prefill forward over the frozen 256-token prompt plus argmax up to the explicit first-token synchronize; the whole prefill compute lives inside the selected Qwen3Model boundary. Measured evidence for the opportunity (nsys diagnostic observations/current/nsys-9ed9145c.json, one invocation, 66441 kernels): the prefill+argmax window is 2146 kernels with 21.34 ms GPU busy against a clean wall of 24.61 ms, i.e. about 3.3 ms of exposed host dispatch; within the busy time ~15.4 ms is cuBLAS/cutlass GEMM plus the 0.83 ms lm_head gemv (near the compute roofline for 2*params*tokens at these shapes, so not the lever), ~0.73 ms flash attention, and ~4.4 ms non-GEMM elementwise/reduce/cat work: 145 RMSNorm sites each as an eager 7-op chain (73 layer norms + 72 q/k head norms), rotary rotate_half with per-layer cat-based rotation, residual adds and SiLU-gated mul (target-resources.json for call 2441f10600ba127de5cb753c: 2144 kernels, 20.75 ms). The candidate replaces this one boundary with a fused composite executed as a single CUDA graph: (a) all hidden-state RMSNorms go through aten rms_norm (fused CUDA path when available), (b) q/k head-norm + rotate-half RoPE collapse into one Triton kernel per tensor that reads the [B,S,H,D] projection output, normalizes per head in fp32, applies RoPE and writes the transposed [B,H,S,D] layout directly, (c) gate SiLU * up fuses into one Triton elementwise kernel, (d) attention calls F.scaled_dot_product_attention directly with the parent's exact configuration for this signature (attn_mask=None, is_causal=True, enable_gqa=True, module scaling), (e) the rotary cos/sin tables, which depend only on positions 0..255 and not on input values, are computed once at installation with the parent's own rotary module, and (f) the whole composite is captured once into a CUDA graph at installation time; every invocation copies the current input_ids into the static buffer and replays, so the workload executes on current inputs each invocation and the ~3.3 ms of exposed per-op dispatch is removed. Expected effect is a hypothesis to be measured: replay removes the exposed dispatch (bound: GPU busy ~21.3 ms) and the fusions target ~2-2.5 ms of the ~4.4 ms non-GEMM busy time, so ttft_ms in the 19-21.5 ms range versus 24.61 ms; decode (31 calls, 11.26 ms GPU busy per step, host-dispatch bound) stays on the parent reference via passthrough, preserving cache growth, continuous execution, reset and the secondary decode_tokens_per_second goal unchanged. The graph is captured from context.references (the current parent callable; no other bundles are installed, search.json buckets empty), so the graph contains the actual parent execution semantics recomputed on each invocation rather than a precomputed answer. Numerical quality: the composite computes the same math with fp32 accumulation and single bf16 rounding inside the fused regions; the project's quality gate is relational (torch.equal greedy tokens and 0.02 logits closeness between the candidate run and its own teacher-forced replay through the same replaced boundary), and both prefill passes are deterministic graph replays, so consistency holds; build-time verification against the eager parent on two random token-id tensors (hidden states and all 36 k/v cache tensors, structural tolerance 0.15) gates the fast path with a fallback ladder composite-graph -> eager-composite -> parent-graph -> parent-eager, each transition reported as a concise setup-failure route label, and any non-matching call signature (different shape/dtype/mask/cache_position-style extras) routes to the parent reference unchanged. A runtime failure on the fast path permanently degrades to parent-eager. Cache semantics across invocations: each prefill returns a fresh DynamicCache view over the graph-static k/v tensors (k contiguous kernel outputs, v strided views), so decode-side torch.cat growth can never alias or go stale between invocations; this wrapper, the decode continuation and second-invocation reuse were validated structurally on CPU (bitwise-identical to the parent with the reference ops, including cache seq-length growth 256->257). No inner call's compute is eliminated: the prefill children execute as native kernels inside the graph rather than as separately dispatched eager Python calls, and the boundary returns the parent's BaseModelOutputWithPast structure, so every consumer (ForCausalLM lm_head slice, adapter argmax, decode cache) remains valid.

setup_work.when: installation (build), outside the measured invocation; no adapter phase context is entered and no fixture-dependent output is stored
steps: Read batch/prompt length from the observed prefill signature in context targets (fallback: state workload), and the module, weights, config and parent reference from context modules/references.

Compute rotary cos/sin tables once with the parent's own rotary module for positions arange(prompt_tokens) (position-only, input-value independent; identical deterministic bf16 values to what the parent recomputes each forward); keep the [S, head_dim/2] halves (~64 KB).
JIT-compile the two Triton kernels on tiny dummy tensors (compile-check; on any failure fall back to equivalent pure-torch ops).
Verify the eager composite against the parent reference on two random token-id tensors: last_hidden_state plus all 36 layers' k/v cache tensors, structural tolerance atol=rtol=0.15.

Side-stream warmup (2 runs) then one CUDA graph capture of the verified callable on a static input buffer; verify two graph replays against fresh eager parent runs on new random inputs; on mismatch or capture failure walk the fallback ladder (eager composite -> parent-eager graph -> parent-eager) with concise setup-failure route labels.
Synchronize and empty the caching allocator's free segments; retain the CUDA graph and its private pool for the model lifetime.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocates a 4 KB static int64 input buffer and ~64 KB of rotary tables, and retains a CUDA graph private pool holding the captured prefill working set plus the static outputs (final hidden state and 36 k/v tensor pairs ~36 MB; total pool on the order of a few hundred MB - exact size is a worker measurement, not claimed here). Verification transients are freed and empty_cache is called. No model parameters are transformed, packed or copied; weights stay shared with the parent module. Retained graph pools increase reserved/lifecycle-reserved memory; per-run peak_allocated_bytes may shift either way since prefill intermediates live in the graph pool - none of these counters is the objective (ttft_ms).
setup_work.approximate_gpu_setup_cost: 3-4 composite/reference prefill runs for verification, 2 warmup runs, 1 capture, 2 replay verifications (~0.3-0.5 s GPU total) plus Triton JIT compile (seconds, host-side)

quality_risks: Fused q/k-norm+RoPE and SiLU*up accumulate in fp32 with a single bf16 rounding per region while the eager parent rounds at every intermediate op: a small deterministic numeric shift versus the parent. The project gate is self-consistent (candidate vs its own teacher-forced replay through the same boundary, logits tolerance 0.02/0.02 and torch.equal greedy tokens), and both prefill passes are deterministic replays on identical inputs, so the shift is far below tolerance; exact greedy-token equality with the original model is expected to hold in practice but is not bitwise-guaranteed by construction.

CUDA Graph replay does not rerun Python hooks: runtime coverage rests on the replacement invocation itself (counted each prefill and each decode step) plus the native kernels executing inside the graph on every invocation; framework traces corroborate the prefill kernel burst as graph launches. Inner prefill children are subsumed by the boundary replacement, not eliminated, and their consumers read the unchanged BaseModelOutputWithPast structure.

Build-time verification and capture can fail on the worker (Triton compile, graph capture of cuBLAS/flash/Triton launches, fused rms_norm availability); every failure path is caught and degrades explicitly - setup-failure route labels for composite-verify / graph-capture / graph-verify, then eager-composite or parent graph or parent-eager - so quality and completion semantics are preserved at reduced speed rather than risking a runtime error.

Cache/state semantics: a fresh DynamicCache view over graph-static k/v tensors is returned per invocation so decode-side cat growth cannot go stale or alias across invocations; validated structurally on CPU including second-invocation reuse and seq-length growth. Decode is pure parent passthrough, so reset(), continuous_steps and the teacher-forced replay keep baseline behavior.

Graph capture happens at installation against the current parent reference with no other bundles installed (binding-contract.md); if a future bundle were installed beneath this boundary, the captured graph would no longer track it and this candidate would need explicit replacement of that bundle's sites.
